title_as_printed: The Bulk and Specific Compressions and Specific Volumes of Aqueous Solutions of Sulfates. Experimental Results over a Pressure Range from 1 to 1000 Bars
pressure_note: Compression k is the volume decrease of 1 cc of solution for a pressure rise from atmospheric (1 bar) to 1000 bars (title: pressure range from 1 to 1000 bars); bars; thermostat 25 +- 0.02 deg.

P.what: upper pressure of the 1 to 1000 bar interval

value.what: bulk compression k = decrease in volume of 1 cc of solution; for water k assumed 0.03935 (393.5 x 10^-4) as basis for all solutions

value2.unit: cm3/g (specific volume of solution at 1 bar, 25 C; unit not printed)
value2.what: specific volume; asterisked values determined by pycnometer by Gibson, the others from International Critical Tables

composition.other_species: Table mixes sulfates: Li2SO4, Na2SO4, Cs2SO4, MgSO4, ZnSO4, CdSO4, BeSO4, (NH4)2SO4, CuSO4, Ce2(SO4)3, H2SO4; only Na2SO4 and MgSO4 are in the six-ion set, others kept as rows. Weight fraction of salt x2 also printed.
composition.volume_basis_evidence: molality; solutions made up directly from weighed amounts of anhydrous salt and water.

skip_rows.reason: second determination line printed below a row: only k (and sometimes specific compression, dPv/x1) given, composition cells blank as printed; values kept in CSV

row_from_literature.reason: specific volume v taken from International Critical Tables (no asterisk); includes pure-water rows

extra_unmapped: psi_2 (derived, effective volume of the solute from Tammann hypothesis)
conversion_needs: H2SO4 concentrations flagged a were computed from density determinations; molality up to 130.8
notes: Stacked blocks as printed; label rows are salt formulas. Last digit of many numbers is printed as a lowered subscript digit; written with a full stop. Pure-water row (x2 = 0) repeated in each block. Where a second line of values is printed below a row (Cs2SO4 k 228.6; (NH4)2SO4 at x2 .15 and .30) it is a separate CSV row with blank composition, and is listed in skip_rows. Printed '....' / '...' kept as '...'.
